changelog: Replace C1 to make high contradiction risk an explicit, primary safety signal and instruct scorers to strongly demote such cuts (addresses the primary finding that contra is underweighted).

Replace example E4 with measured labeled example en_us_738 demonstrating a cut that isolates negation/scope ('does not issue ... more than one month'), so scorers learn to penalize cuts that separate scope-bearing words from their complements.
findings: The prompt underweights high contradiction risk: it ranks cuts highly even when the pre-cut fragment, read alone, becomes a plausible but misleading or contradicted claim (scope/negation/complement appears after the cut).
The prompt lacks concrete examples showing how to penalize cuts that isolate scope-bearing words (negation, quantifiers, 'except', comparatives) so scorers favor cohesion over safety.

diagnosis.why: Making high-contradiction risk an explicit, primary signal (C1) — reinforced by the negation example swap (E4) — caused scorers to avoid cuts that isolate negation/scope or obvious contradiction sites and instead shift cuts to other, weaker junctions (e.g., splitting function words and list items). That redistribution produced a small net loss in H_set (n_worse>n_better) concentrated in longer-latency bins (≤10 and ≤99) with modest harm also for the shortest pieces (≤3), matching the by_bin pattern.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep contradiction-risk demotion but avoid prompting scorers to systematically relocate cuts into positions that split function words or enumerations and thereby reduce cohesion for longer-latency cut sets.
